key_insight: The paper argues that under a fixed per-query budget, LLM systems should dynamically split spending between resampling the current model and rerouting to another model, because the best choice depends on verifier confidence and instance-level recoverability.
engineering_relevance: For deployed LLM serving, this provides a practical budget-aware policy for improving answer quality without simply increasing cost, especially in heterogeneous model pools.
method: Formulate test-time model selection as a budget allocation problem between resampling and rerouting.
Use an online RoR policy that estimates marginal correctness per unit cost.
Ground the policy in recoverability asymmetry and compare against routing, best-of-K, cascade, and random baselines.
evidence_signal: Replay experiments on regenerated multi-draw correctness tensors from an 11-model pool across four benchmarks show RoR yields a stronger cost-quality Pareto front, with the biggest gains on the most heterogeneous benchmark.
watch_item: The gains depend on verifier quality and shrink substantially when the verifier becomes weaker, so deployment requires a reliable verifier or careful robustness checks.
paper_title: Resample or Reroute? Budget-Aware Test-Time Model Selection for Large Language Models
